Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using blanket thickness measurements as a leading indicator.  
Departure: In-situ blanket strain calculation via differential pressure across the blanket cylinder, derived from existing press sensors.  
Failure-physics connection: Swelling increases internal stress, altering pressure distribution; strain correlates with registration drift before dimensional changes are detectable.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Strain (ε) = ΔP / (E * t), where ΔP is pressure differential, E is Young’s modulus (stated spec: 10 MPa), t is blanket thickness (stated spec: 1.6 mm).  
Magnitude verification: For 5% swelling, ΔP = 0.05 * 10e6 Pa * 1.6e-3 m = 800 Pa (CALCULATED, from stated specs).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Pressure transducers: Existing blanket cylinder pressure sensors (ALREADY-RECORDED, "stated telemetry feed").  
- Strain calculation unit: Firmware update (existing press controller).  
- Threshold: 0.5% strain (CALCULATED, from 800 Pa ΔP / (10e6 Pa * 1.6e-3 m)).  
- Reference: Baseline ΔP from startup (ALREADY-RECORDED, "stated log").  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as existing sensor integration (no new hardware).  
- Operability: Automated calculation in existing HMI (no operator training).  
- Maintenance: Zero additional burden (uses existing sensors).  
- Cost class: Identical to standard practice (no new materials/services).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Record ΔP during 10,000-sheet run; calculate strain every 1,000 sheets.  
Pass/fail: Threshold = 0.5% strain; fail if exceeded.  
Duration: 1 job cycle.  
Kill criterion: Registration drift > 0.5mm (stated failure metric).  
Validation: Against ALREADY-RECORDED data from prior runs (stated log).  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Registration drift (defines failure per problem statement). Supplement: Strain (predictive, not replacement).  

RISK: Pressure differential may not fully capture localized swelling; requires validation against historical failure data.
